question: How many US banks will fail in November or December 2026?

calls.reasoning: Six US bank failures Jan-Sep 2026 (four since July), no October failure found through Oct 28. Poisson at the 2026 pace gives lambda~1.1-1.3 for the two-month window. The 2017-2025 Nov-Dec history (about 3 of 9 windows had one failure, none had 2+) and fewer usable Fridays around the holidays pull toward 0/1. Thin Manifold full-year market '7+ failures in 2026' at ~0.51 implies roughly 50% chance of at least one more failure in Oct 28-Dec 31, a near-miss that also counts late October. No Polymarket/Kalshi market on this exact contract. Blend with overdispersion lands at ~64% for at least one failure.
calls.dossier:
- FDIC Failed Bank List (fetched 2026-10-28, page last updated 2026-09-25): 2026 failures = Metropolitan Capital Bank & Trust, Chicago IL (Jan 30); Community Bank and Trust-West Georgia, LaGrange GA (May 1); Kentland Federal S&L, Kentland IN (Jul 10); Small Business Bank, Lenexa KS (Jul 17); Tioga-Franklin Savings Bank, Philadelphia PA (Aug 21); Nano Banc, Irvine CA (Sep 25, $736M assets).
- 2025 failures per FDIC list: Pulaski Savings Bank (Jan 17), Santa Anna National Bank (Jun 27); none in Nov-Dec 2025.
- Disruption Banking 2026-10-01: six failures in 2026 = most in a decade; marketintellabs: ~$1.43B assets, ~$243M DIF cost as of Oct 6. All small community banks; described as a steady 'drip', no systemic event.
- Searches for an October 2026 failure (as of Oct 28) found none.
- 2026 YTD pace: 6 failures in ~9 months (0.67/month); 4 of 6 in Jul-Sep (higher recent pace). Naive Poisson over 2 months: lambda ~1.1-1.3.
- Historical Nov-Dec windows 2017-2025 (from memory, partly unverified): 2017 one (Washington Federal Bank for Savings, Dec 15), 2019 one (City National Bank of NJ, Nov 1), 2023 one (Citizens Bank Sac City, Nov 3), other years zero; no window with 2+. Over this low-failure era: about 3/9 windows with exactly 1, 6/9 with 0.
- FDIC closures usually happen on Fridays; the late-December holidays reduce usable Fridays.
- Resolution: resolves off the FDIC Failed Bank List closing dates only; event window Nov 1, 2026 -> Dec 31, 2026; as of Oct 28, 0% elapsed. An Oct 30 failure would not count.
- Markets: Manifold has thin full-year 2026 total-count markets (7+, 8+, 9+, 10+); no Polymarket/Kalshi contract on Nov-Dec counts found.
- Searched for but not found: FDIC Q3 2026 problem-bank list count, specific named troubled banks under enforcement action.
calls.reference_class: Nov-Dec two-month windows of US FDIC bank failures 2017-2025, combined with a Poisson rate from 2026 YTD failures

calls.reasoning: FDIC list shows 6 failures in 2026 through Oct 28 (last: Nano Banc Sep 25), ~0.6/month, implying Poisson lambda ~1.2 for a 2-month window; trimmed toward ~1.0 because Nov-Dec failures were rare in 2019-2025 and December holiday timing may slow closures. Poisson(1.0) gives ~.37/.37/.18/.08. Manifold annual-count ladder (7+/8+/9+ at .51/.31/.15, thin volume, includes late-Oct window) implies ~.49/.20/.16/.15 for the Nov-Dec counts; used as near-miss evidence, not an anchor. Blended toward slightly more mass on 0 and a fatter tail than pure Poisson for overdispersion (Jul-Aug 2026 had 3).

calls.reasoning: Six small-bank failures in 2026 through Oct 28 (latest Nano Banc, Sep 25; none found in October). The 2026 pace of ~0.6/month implies lambda ~1.2 for Nov-Dec. Pulling down: 2017-2025 Nov-Dec windows had at most one failure each, problem banks fell 54->47 in Q2 2026, and holiday weeks leave fewer closure Fridays. Pulling up: four failures came in Jul-Sep. Used lambda ~0.95 with overdispersion. The Manifold full-year ladders (thin; window includes late October) imply ~50% for at least one more failure, consistent with this.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the facts: 6 failures in 2026 through Sep 25, none in October, problem banks at 47, Manifold ladder at 7+ 0.51 / 8+ 0.31 / 9+ 0.15. I checked for an October 2026 failure: the search returned only the six known failures, with Nano Banc on Sep 25 the latest. The disagreement is how much weight the high 2026 pace (lambda 1.2) gets against the low Nov-Dec history (~0.3) and the falling problem-bank count. That is a judgment call. I took lambda ~0.95 with some overdispersion, near Run 2.
